findings.issue: payloadHierarchyRows marks a node `last` when it is immediately followed by a SIBLING at the same depth, which breaks the drawn tree guides into floating segments — the exact failure HierarchyRow's KDoc exists to warn about. The accompanying test asserts the bug and its comment rationalises it.
findings.description: HierarchyOutline.kt:75 computes `last = next == null || next.depth <= node.depth`. HierarchyRow draws this node's own-column branch as `drawLine(branchX, 0 -> if (last) midY else size.height)` (HierarchyRow.kt:109-116) while every descendant AND every later same-depth sibling redraws a full-height line at that same branchX. So `last` must mean 'nothing below continues in my column'. A following sibling at the same depth DOES continue it, so the correct predicate is `next == null || next.depth < node.depth` (strict). With `<=`, every non-final sibling stops its guide at midY and leaves a half-row gap before the next sibling's branch begins. The pre-existing reference usage confirms the intent: StyleguideScreen.kt:743-745 deliberately leaves the non-final depth-1 row `last = false` and only the final sibling `last = true`. In a real ~400-node uiautomator dump most nodes have a following sibling, so AC-15's 'monospace indented tree' renders as a field of disconnected dashes rather than a tree.
findings.evidence: presentation-feature-mirror/.../core/payload/HierarchyOutline.kt:75 `last = next == null || next.depth <= node.depth` | presentation-core-ui/.../molecule/row/HierarchyRow.kt:109-116 (branch drawn to `if (last) midY else size.height`) and its `last` KDoc at HierarchyRow.kt:50-54 | presentation-core-ui/.../showcase/StyleguideScreen.kt:743-745 (reference tree: only the final sibling is `last = true`) | HierarchyOutlineTest.kt:65-67 asserts `item_a` (depth 1, immediately followed by sibling `item_b` at depth 1) has `last = true`, with the comment at :61-64 rationalising it as 'each one's own column guide ends right there, regardless of sibling order' — the test re-states the implementation's rule instead of the component's contract, so 251 green mirror tests cannot catch this.

findings.issue: The AC-80 / SC-23 no-hierarchy state is unreachable in the combination production actually produces: HierarchyStatus.Unavailable is reduced while a FULL snapshot is published to frozenHierarchy, and PayloadHierarchySection's `when` tests `rows.isNotEmpty()` first — so the tab renders a several-hundred-node unbadged tree under a readout that says 'no hierarchy'.
findings.description: MirrorViewModel.dumpHierarchyFor (MirrorViewModel.kt:407-421) sets `currentFrozenHierarchy.value = snapshot` BEFORE reducing, then reduces `Unavailable` whenever `projectMeasureNodes(snapshot, frozenSize).isEmpty()`. Its own KDoc (MirrorViewModel.kt:396-404) names the live cause: a dump that succeeds but whose frame size disagrees with the frozen frame — the T-1 spike measured a 9.76% gap between uiautomator's reported size and the physical screen, so this is a measured, recurring device condition, not a hypothetical. In that state MirrorPayloadTab receives `hierarchy` with hundreds of nodes plus `hierarchyStatus == Unavailable`. payloadHierarchyRows returns one row per node, all unbadged (HierarchyOutlineTest.aMismatchedFrameSizeStillProducesARowPerNodeWithNoBadges proves exactly this). PayloadHierarchySection then takes its first branch and renders the whole LazyColumn tree — every row at ink3 because nothing is `matched` — while hierarchySourceLabel(Unavailable, nodeCount) prints 'no hierarchy' beside the label. AC-80 requires 'shows zero nodes and an explicit no-hierarchy state rather than an empty tree that looks like a bug'; what ships is the opposite failure (a full tree contradicting its own readout). The section's KDoc (MirrorPayloadTab.kt:558-561) states 'Absent and Unavailable get an explicit line saying so' unconditionally — behaviour the code does not have, since that branch only runs when rows are empty.
findings.evidence: MirrorViewModel.kt:407-410 `val snapshot = dumpHierarchy(deviceId).getOrNull(); currentFrozenHierarchy.value = snapshot ?: HierarchySnapshotModel.Empty` then :413-419 `val usable = snapshot != null && projectMeasureNodes(...).isNotEmpty(); hierarchyStatus = if (usable) Ready else Unavailable` | MirrorPayloadTab.kt:594-616 `when { rows.isNotEmpty() -> LazyColumn(...); status == Absent || status == Unavailable -> Text(no-hierarchy) }` | MirrorPayloadTab.kt:896-916: the AC-80 preview pair — the spec's declared PRIMARY evidence for AC-80 — pins `hierarchy = HierarchySnapshotModel.Empty` alongside `hierarchyStatus = Unavailable`, i.e. it demonstrates only the combination that cannot fail and never the one production emits.

findings.issue: The new `matched: Boolean = false` parameter silently changed the shipped appearance of a public shared component: HierarchyRow node labels were unconditionally Theme.color.ink and are now ink3 unless the caller opts in. The three pre-existing call sites were not updated.
findings.description: The parameter is additive in signature but NOT additive in behaviour. StyleguideScreen.kt:743-745 renders three HierarchyRows with no `matched` argument, so the showcase hierarchy now reads de-emphasised — including the rows carrying `tag = "#1"` and `tag = "#2"`, producing a tagged-but-grey state that the new KDoc declares impossible ('Matched nodes read at full ink; the rest of the dump recedes to ink3 so the matches stand out'). A tag is the component's own marker for 'an annotation matched this node', so a tagged ink3 row is self-contradictory. There is no Compose UI-test harness in this repo and HierarchyRow has no test at all, so nothing would catch it; the only reason it did not surface is that the affected screen is the internal styleguide. The lazy fix is to pass `matched = true` wherever a `tag` is passed at the existing call sites, or to derive the ink from `tag != null` inside the component so the two can never disagree.
findings.evidence: git diff sdd/measure-mode...HEAD -- HierarchyRow.kt: `- color = Theme.color.ink` / `+ color = if (matched) Theme.color.ink else Theme.color.ink3` (HierarchyRow.kt:125) | presentation-core-ui/.../showcase/StyleguideScreen.kt:743-745 — three call sites, zero `matched` arguments, two of them carrying `tag` | presentation-core-ui desktopTest has 29 tests and none of them touch HierarchyRow.

findings.issue: Crop cells are FITTED to a constant (CropCellWidth = 84.dp) but DRAWN in a weighted box whose real width is (panelWidth - 32dp)/3. At PanelMinWidth the crop and the right edge of its red outline are clipped; at PanelMaxWidth ~44% of each cell is empty, left-anchored. cropWindow's KDoc claim that the cell size 'changes only when the window moves to a different display' is false.
findings.description: PayloadCropsSection passes `boxW = CropCellWidth.toPx()` (84.dp) into cropWindow, but each PayloadCropCell is laid out with `Modifier.weight(1f)`, its Box is `fillMaxWidth().height(CropCellHeight)` and the Canvas is `matchParentSize()`. The real cell width is therefore (panelWidth - 2*spacingS tab padding - 2*spacingS gaps)/3. With ShellWindowDefaults.PanelMinWidth = 260.dp that is (260-16-16)/3 ~= 76.dp, 8.dp narrower than the 84.dp the window was fitted for: the drawImage dstSize and the outlineRect (both anchored at dstOffset = IntOffset.Zero) overrun the Canvas and the right ~10% of the crop plus the right edge of the red outline are clipped away, so AC-14's 'cropped image with its red outline baked in' and AC-76's exact outline placement are both visually broken at minimum panel width. With PanelMaxWidth = 480.dp the cell is ~149.dp and each crop sits in the top-left of a cell that is 65.dp too wide — the KDoc's 'a cell a few dp wider than this shows the slack on its right' understates it by an order of magnitude. The geometry is only correct near PanelDefaultWidth = 300.dp (~89.dp cell). CropWindowTest's assertOutlineInsideDst guarantees containment in `dstSize` only, never containment in the cell actually drawn, so the unit suite cannot see this. Lazy fix: hand cropWindow the measured cell width (BoxWithConstraints / onSizeChanged) instead of the design constant, or give each cell `Modifier.width(CropCellWidth)` and stop weighting.
findings.evidence: MirrorPayloadTab.kt:409-422 (`cellWidth = CropCellWidth.toPx()` fed as `boxW`) vs MirrorPayloadTab.kt:448-456 (`PayloadCropCell(..., modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))`) and :501-508 (`fillMaxWidth().height(CropCellHeight)` + `Canvas(matchParentSize())`) | MirrorPayloadTab.kt:124-127 CropCellWidth = 84.dp with the KDoc that claims only-wider | presentation-core-ui/.../ShellWindowDefaults.kt:23,26,29 PanelMinWidth 260.dp / PanelMaxWidth 480.dp / PanelDefaultWidth 300.dp | ThemeSpacing.kt:11 spacingS = 8.dp | core/payload/CropWindow.kt:43-45 KDoc 'it is a density conversion of two constants, so it changes only when the window moves to a different display'.

findings.issue: PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION is dead code with a tautological test, and its KDoc documents a consumer that does not exist.
findings.description: The constant is referenced exactly once in the whole repository outside its own declaration: by PayloadEstimateTest:160 `assertEquals(1, PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION)`, which compares a compile-time constant to its own literal and can therefore only fail if someone edits the constant and forgets the test — it asserts no behaviour. Nothing in the tree serialises, encodes or exports a payload, so the KDoc's 'a reader on the other side keys its parsing off this number' describes a reader that does not exist. No AC in this spec mentions a format version. Lazy resolution: delete both the constant and its test, and reintroduce them in the deliverable that actually writes the wire format.

findings.issue: AC-16's literal wording — 'a total size that matches the actual payload' — is not met and is not meetable in this deliverable: nothing encodes or exports a payload, and payloadSizeLabel is an admitted linear heuristic.
findings.description: I inspected this one (verificationMethod: inspection). PayloadFooter reads footerLabel(count) and payloadSizeLabel(count) straight from core/payload with no re-derivation, which is the property the task was really after: the readout and any future exporter share one function, so a displayed size that disagrees with the computed one is not expressible. But the function is `1.6 + 0.12*count MB` with its own KDoc conceding 'the real size is not known until the frame is encoded', and AC-78 blesses that exact formula. So AC-16 and AC-78 are mutually inconsistent as written in the plan; AC-16 is satisfied only in the weaker 'single source of truth' sense. Flagging so the human gate records which reading was accepted rather than discovering it at export time.
findings.evidence: core/payload/PayloadEstimate.kt:11-15,34-40 (SIZE_BASE_MB 1.6, SIZE_PER_CROP_MB 0.12, KDoc 'Also a heuristic; the real size is not known until the frame is encoded') | MirrorPayloadTab.kt:663-668 PayloadFooter | plan.json AC-16 vs AC-78.

findings.issue: The badge-to-annotation coupling is implicit and untested: payloadHierarchyRows discards StagedAnnotation.index and re-derives badges as `position + 1`, while PayloadPromptSection matches them back with `row.badge == annotation.index`.
findings.description: The two agree today only because stageAnnotation assigns `index = frozen.annotations.size + 1` and deleteAnnotation renumbers survivors to `position + 1`. If that invariant ever slips, the prompt silently loses every node id (nodeIdFor returns null for all annotations) and the badges in the tree no longer correspond to the `#N` in the prompt — a silent degradation, not a failure. No test pins the row badge and the prompt's node id together for a non-trivially-numbered annotation list. The lazy fix is to pass `List<StagedAnnotation>` (or a list of index/rect pairs) into payloadHierarchyRows so the real index travels with the rect instead of being reconstructed.
findings.evidence: HierarchyOutline.kt:63-66 (`annotations.forEachIndexed { position, ... } ... getOrPut(it.id) { position + 1 }`, parameter type `List<DeviceRect>`) | MirrorPayloadTab.kt:294 `rows.firstOrNull { row -> row.badge == annotation.index }?.nodeId` | MirrorViewModel.kt:373 and :518-519 (the two places that keep index == position + 1).

findings.issue: PayloadNodeRow.matched duplicates `badge != null`; the data class permits constructing a row where the two disagree.
findings.description: Its own KDoc admits the field is derived ('`badge != null`, named for the renderer's benefit'). It is only ever constructed as `matched = badge != null`, so no live inconsistency exists — but it is two fields encoding one fact in a type that a future caller can build by hand. A computed `val matched: Boolean get() = badge != null` would make the duplication unrepresentable for the same line count.

findings.issue: Six ACs with verificationMethod: test have an automated logic half and a UI half proven only by @Preview pairs that nobody has opened. A preview is not evidence until a human looks at it.
findings.description: The repo has no Compose UI-test harness and a DoD line forbids adding one, so this is a structural ceiling rather than an executor omission. Per AC: AC-13 — buildPrompt and tokenEstimate are tested; that the Prompt block actually renders the estimate and the Edit affordance is preview-only. AC-14 — cropWindow is tested to 8 hand-computed cases; the 3-column grid rendering is preview-only (and see AF-4). AC-15 — payloadHierarchyRows is tested; the rendered tree is preview-only (and see AF-1, AF-3: both of this audit's errors live exactly in that unverified half). AC-72 — PromptAssemblyTest.dimensionPairIsUnspacedTimesNeverTheSpacePaddedSizeLabel covers the prompt; the crop caption's glyph is preview-only (string-level inspection confirms MirrorPayloadTab.kt:535-536 interpolates TIMES with no spaces and calls no formatter). AC-78 — tokenEstimate/payloadSizeLabel are tested at 18 cases; 'recompute synchronously with no measurable lag' is satisfied by construction (both are read inline from `count`, O(1), no cache to invalidate) and by inspection, not by measurement. AC-79 — the override's reducer half is tested at 8 cases; that clicking Edit swaps in MultilineInput and that `promptOverride ?: generated` is what renders is preview-only.
